newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK car sales seen up, China fall continuing-report.
newsitem.headline: HK car sales seen up, China fall continuing-report.

text.p: Car sales in Hong Kong posted a year high in October with strong numbers seen for the rest of 1996 but sales in China are likely to remain depressed in the near future, Schroders Securities said on Tuesday.
The October car sales of 2,176 vehicles suggested the upward trend was robust and should bring the total sales for the year to about 23,000 against 22,881 in 1995, it said in a report.
This compared with a 29.4 percent fall year-on-year in 1995.
"Despite our enthusiastic outlook for Hong Kong's car sales, we wish to warn investors that car sales in China for the near future are likey to remain depressed," the report said.
Hong Kong car dealers in China were being hit by falling prices, slow demand and a proliferation of smuggled vehicles, the brokerage said.
